appId.description: Stable identifier: lowercase letters, digits, dots and dashes.

version.description: The app's version, returned by app.version(). Defaults to package.json's version.

width.description: Initial window width in logical pixels.

height.description: Initial window height in logical pixels.

minWidth.description: Smallest width the user can resize the window to, in logical pixels.

minHeight.description: Smallest height the user can resize the window to, in logical pixels.

maxWidth.description: Largest width the user can resize the window to, in logical pixels.

maxHeight.description: Largest height the user can resize the window to, in logical pixels.

resizable.description: Whether the user can resize the window.

center.description: Center the window on first launch. A remembered position takes precedence.

decorations.description: Show the system title bar and borders. Turn off for a frameless window.

titleBarStyle.description: macOS only. "transparent" shows the window background through the title bar; "overlay" also lets the page draw under it (mark a drag region with data-tauri-drag-region). Other platforms always show a normal title bar.

rememberWindow.description: Reopen the window at the size, position and maximized state the user left it in.

frontend.description: A directory with index.html, or a Vite setup.

native.description: Native functions module (native.ts or native.js), run inside the host.

csp.description: Content-Security-Policy for the built app (never applied in dev). Omit for Kestrel's default: scripts only from the app, no eval. An empty string turns it off.

permissions.description: Capabilities the app's webview std-lib and native code may use. Omit or leave empty for none: no files, clipboard, notifications or links.

oneOf.description: Read and write files inside the app's data directory. Relative paths resolve there.
Read and write files and folders the user picks in a dialog (dialog.pickFile, pickFolder, save).
Read and write any file the user can. Relative paths still resolve in the app's data directory. Prefer fs:app-data or fs:pick.
Read and write the clipboard's text (clipboard.readText, writeText).
Open http, https and mailto links in the default app (shell.open).
